prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a general, mechanistically understood transformation (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination, with ligand design controlling each step) used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. Buchwald and Hartwig independently built the ligand families that made it broadly applicable, so a two-name credit follows the real history without trimming. About 25 to 30 years of independent confirmation and industrial adoption mean the interpretation is stable. After round 1 this remains the only shortlisted candidate where the three questions the committee has to settle (is the achievement one coherent thing, who exactly did it, is it settled) all have short answers. The round-1 exchange did not change that, and the chair's summary shows that the committee's main open problem is B037 attribution and maturity, not any weakness in B005.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is still the relation to the 2010 cross-coupling prize: a sceptic can call this a second Pd-coupling award for a different bond. My answer is that C-N bond formation needed its own ligand classes and its own mechanistic work on amine binding and C-N reductive elimination, which is a distinct achievement, but I accept this is a judgement and not a fact that settles the matter. The Kosugi and Migita tin-amide precursor remains unresolved and a two-name citation leaves it out; wording around the general catalytic method, not first observation, is the honest way to handle it. Hartwig's appearance on another candidate is a minor point. Finally, B005 is the safe choice, and the committee should ask whether safe is a sufficient reason when a more transformative idea is nearly ready.

responses.point: Chabes argued that approval of a drug is not the right test for a chemistry prize: the first PROTAC dates to 2001, cereblon as the thalidomide target to 2010, and the induced-proximity claim is settled and widely reproduced.
responses.response: I accept this and I withdraw the framing in my round-1 reply to Linke that clinical approval is the main test. The scientific claim, that proximity to an E3 ligase drives catalytic removal of a target, is established, and approval status alone should not decide a chemistry prize. My remaining objection to B037 is different and I think it is not answered by the maturity argument: the PROTAC strand (Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray) and the cereblon strand (Handa, Ito, Kim) have different logic and different histories, and a trio drawn from both is a choice made to fit a three-name limit. You list the same omissions yourself. Until the committee can say why Handa and Deshaies should be preferred to Sakamoto and Ciulli on scientific grounds, and not on grounds of convenience, I cannot rank it above B005.

responses.point: Linke, as chair and first-place supporter of B037, says the two-strand structure (PROTAC concept; cereblon and glues) maps onto three names with a defensible attribution logic, while admitting that his ranking may reflect an appealing story.
responses.response: I take your candour about the story seriously, and I agree that the idea is original. The mapping onto three names is where I still disagree. If the citation is one achievement, induced proximity, then the credit should follow who established it, and that is Crews, Deshaies and Sakamoto for the first PROTAC and Ciulli for making the concept general with VHL ligands. If the citation is cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type glues, that is Handa, Ito and Kim and a different prize part. Your citation names both, which suggests the committee has not yet decided what the discovery is. I would rather you specify that before asking the other members to vote on it. If you can show that one reading is clearly dominant, I would reconsider.

responses.point: Aili argued that B005 extends the logic honoured in 2010 to another bond, whereas genetic code expansion (B002) and base editing (B060) open qualitatively new capabilities, while conceding that B005 would be safer if attribution is the decisive criterion.
responses.response: The novelty argument is fair and I have partly adopted it by keeping B002 as an alternative. My difficulty with your two-part configuration is the attribution you identify yourself: the B002 cut leaves out Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama, whose early experimental work you describe as genuinely shared, and B060 has the Nishida and Kondo parallel report. Two uncertain credit boundaries in one configuration is a larger risk than one. On whether C-N coupling is a repeat of 2010, I would say a prize is judged by what had to be invented. For C-N coupling that was a new ligand design and a mechanistic understanding of amine binding and reductive elimination, not an extension of conditions. I accept that this is a judgement and that you may weigh it differently.

responses.point: Aqvist said that C-N coupling is constrained rather than overdue because it extends the 2010 logic, whereas Car-Parrinello opened a new capability, and that he would not fight a Buchwald-Hartwig prize.
responses.response: I agree that B016 is the cleaner invention and the one with no predecessor, and I would not oppose it. Where I stay with B005 is the question of how much the committee has already recognised in the area: DFT in 1998 and multiscale modelling in 2013 are close neighbours of Car-Parrinello,, so another computational prize may be a harder sell. With your note that you would accept B005, the two of us have the same fallback, which matters more than the order. I would also keep Parrinello's later work out of the citation and tie it to the 1985 invention, as you suggest.

responses.point: Zou agrees on maturity and two-person attribution and would word the citation around the general catalytic method, not first discovery, because Kosugi's precursor is a real priority issue.
responses.response: I agree with the wording, and I have kept my citation to the development of the catalytic method for that reason. I would also keep the point I made in round 1: we are both Stockholm University colleagues and we are likely to share the same recollection of the priority record, so our agreement is not independent evidence. The committee's expert reports on Kosugi and Migita should be checked by someone who has not already settled on the answer.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize.
How to word the citation so that Kosugi and Migita precursor chemistry is respected without adding a third name.
Whether the committee can state a single clear achievement for B037 and justify its trio on scientific grounds; if it can, my ordering could change.
Whether a first regulatory approval of a PROTAC before the decision would change the B037 maturity argument.
statement.conflict_note: I am a Stockholm University colleague of committee member Xiaodong Zou, and I serve as Secretary and Nobel Foundation board deputy. None of the shortlisted candidates is from my institution or a collaborator of mine, and my field (biological energy conversion) is not close to any credited person, so no specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. This is unchanged from round 1.
